sections.what_happened: [VERIFIED FACT -- vessel identification] The tanker in Wednesday's Hormuz mine incident (recorded 1400-02, vessel unnamed) is the NCC Fajr, a Saudi-flagged Bahri product tanker (81,300-dwt, built 2013), carrying 3 Indian seafarers; all crew safe, per Indian Ports Minister Sarbananda Sonowal on X (via Khaleej Times 16:19 ; TradeWinds updated 11:50Z). Maritime intelligence firm Vanguard Tech linked the UKMTO incident to a 'possible attack' on the NCC Fajr. It is the THIRD Bahri-owned ship hit in/near the Gulf per TradeWinds calculations; 16 Bahri ships sit on an Iranian blacklist of vessels making Hormuz transits without Tehran's approval. [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM -- IRGC 'two more'] Separately, the IRGC Navy claimed Wednesday (IRNA 12:27Z = 16:27 , in-window) that TWO MORE tankers hit naval mines after switching off navigation/identification systems and attempting to leave Hormuz via an unauthorised route 'under the cover of US terrorist military forces'. No vessel names, flags or crew details given; no second UKMTO report; no independent corroboration. IRGC also claims US coastal radar/navigational aids south of the strait were destroyed, raising risks for tankers on unauthorised routes. TALLY WARNING: Tuesday's IRGC 'two/three tankers' claims, Wednesday morning's one tanker (NCC Fajr) and Wednesday's 'two more' claim overlap in counting and must NOT be summed into a confirmed total. PortWatch snapshot 2026-11-11 NOT stale (latest observation Nov 8, 3-day lag): Hormuz 3 transits Nov 8, 7-day avg 3.86 vs 2025 baseline 85.53/day (4.5% of baseline).
sections.what_verified: NCC Fajr identification: 2 tiered families (UKMTO T1; Indian Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways T1 STATE IN) + 2 untiered carriers (TradeWinds, Khaleej Times -- do not count toward corroboration). IRGC 'two more' claim: 1 family only -- IRNA (T3, STATE IR), the primary source of its own statement.
sections.what_disputed: US military recently claimed all mines had been cleared from the strait (recorded 1400-02) -- directly contradicts the mine-strike cause; no US response to today's claims yet. CENTCOM said last month it helped Gulf countries export 1.5bn barrels via Hormuz since summer -- its escort claim stands against Iran's restriction claim, while PortWatch counted only 3 transits on Nov 8.
sections.why_matters: Named at last: the tanker Iran mined in Hormuz this morning is Saudi Arabia's NCC Fajr -- the THIRD Bahri ship hit -- and Tehran now claims two more. The strait that carries a fifth of the world's oil saw 3 ships pass on Nov 8.
sections.context: Background: Hormuz -- Wednesday mine incident vessel named NCC Fajr (Saudi-flagged Bahri tanker, 3 Indian seafarers safe); IRGC claims two MORE tankers hit mines

totw_analysis: Our read: Named at last: the tanker Iran mined in Hormuz this morning is Saudi Arabia's NCC Fajr -- the THIRD Bahri ship hit -- and Tehran now claims two more. The strait that carries a fifth of the world's oil saw 3 ships pass on Nov 8. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Iran calls the NCC Fajr a 'violating' tanker on an unauthorised route; Bahri and the US call it a lawful transit under escort. Who writes the rules for the world's oil artery -- Tehran's blacklist or the US Navy's escorts?
